messages:
maria_support: Hey team — acme reported a big latency spike this morning and that some of their traffic suddenly started hitting EU instead of us-west. They saw a bunch of 401s and a billing jump. Can someone triage?

jon_eng_oncall: looking now. any sample request ids or timestamps?

maria_support: sent logs in thread: request ids `req_8f3a` `req_8f4b`. spike ~2799899950 -> 2799900000. customer says it started right after they updated a routing policy in the console.

lee_infra: quick grep of router logs shows a bubbling of fallback hits to eu-1 between 2799899940-2799900060 for that api_key (acct: acme). many requests returned 401 from eu-1 auth proxy.

olivia_prod: note: there was a config migrate job that ran at 2799899930 that normalized affinity configs (stringify weights). the migration script had a small change to how "seed" is encoded in cookie-affinity entries. rolling it back might help.

jon_eng_oncall: can you paste the before/after of the affinity fragment?

olivia_prod: sure — before (live pre-migrate):
```json
{"cookie_affinity": {"enabled": true, "seed": 12345, "priority": ["us-west","eu-1"], "weights": [80,20]}}
```
after migrate (what we wrote to the store):
```json
{"cookie_affinity": {"enabled": true, "seed": "12345", "priority": ["eu-1","us-west"], "weights": ["20","80"]}}
```

maria_support: so seed became a string and priority array order flipped? customer insists they didn't change priority.

lee_infra: parity check: runtime decoder treats seed as numeric when computing the hash modulo ring-size. If seed is a string we currently coerce differently (we hash the JSON string), which can change affinity buckets. Also the priority order flip would change fallback evaluation order if we mis-parsed the migration output.

jon_eng_oncall: that explains cross-region hits. why 401s though?

lee_infra: eu-1 auth proxy uses a different token validation cluster that only sees the customer's us-west token for a short TTL. If sticky routing flips mid-session, some requests land in eu-1 where the token has already been invalidated by that cluster's cache -> 401.

maria_support: customer also flagged a billing surge; does cross-region routing affect billing?

sophie_billing: yes — egress rates and per-region pricing differ. If requests route to eu-1 unexpectedly we can see a sudden egress/billing delta. we'll flag for investigation but suggest limiting further customer impact first.

jon_eng_oncall: immediate remediation: 1) pause the migrate job and roll back the config store to the snapshot at 2799899900. 2) add a hotfix to the runtime decoder to coerce numeric-string seeds into numbers until a permanent fix. 3) roll out a config fix to restore original priority order for affected customers.

lee_infra: I can roll back store snapshot now. kicking it off. deploy_bot: started snapshot-rollback job id snap-2799899900

deploy_bot: snapshot-rollback job snap-2799899900 started by lee_infra — ETA ~40s

jon_eng_oncall: while rollback runs — can someone craft repro steps so we can validate fix and confirm bill/latency stop? need exact curl + headers + cookie behavior.

maria_support: adding repro steps I gave to customer earlier (condensed):
1) set affinity cookie (redwood_aff) with value computed from user id e.g. `u:42`
2) send 100 requests with header `X-Api-Key: <their-key>` spaced 50ms
3) watch host header / region in response and token validation responses

I also included a small script:```bash
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -b "redwood_aff=u:42" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate; sleep 0.05; done
```

olivia_prod: rollback finished. store now matches snapshot. runtime still needs hotfix; currently many routing decisions rely on seed parsing at decode time.

jon_eng_oncall: restarting a small cohort of router pods to pick up store snapshot now (canary). lee?

lee_infra: canary restart started for router-pool-canary-71 -> will monitor metrics (latency, cross-region hits, 401s).

deploy_bot: canary deploy health: metrics stable -> slight drop in eu-1 hits (down 75%)

maria_support: customer ran the repro and reports region stabilized to us-west and 401s stopped. they say latency back to normal. :relieved:

sophie_billing: billing team: I captured the egress delta for acct acme — looks like ~3.2% spike while misrouting lasted (~90s). we'll adjust invoice if needed; please attach timeline to the ticket.

jon_eng_oncall: follow-ups: 1) patch migration script to preserve numeric types for seed/weights and never reorder priority arrays unless explicitly changed (PR opened) 2) add unit tests to detect type coercion 3) add a quick invariant check in runtime that warns when store types don't match expected schema (log + metric) 4) run a customer-impact audit and offer credit if billing exceed threshold.

olivia_prod: PR: https://git.internal/r/prod/migrations/encode-seed-fix (notes added). also adding a small canary test that runs a simulated affinity hash against migrated configs.

lee_infra: logged incident for postmortem (INC-27999). capturing traces, router logs, and migration diffs.

maria_support: closing loop with customer now. will offer a short credit and summary of actions, and ask them to confirm they are good.

jon_eng_oncall: thanks all. main root cause: migration changed seed type + reordered priority array for some customers -> cookie-affinity hash produced different bucket -> sticky routing flipped regions -> token validation mismatch produced 401s and some billing/egress exposure. mitigation done (rollback + canary + migration fix + runtime guard).

maria_support: marking resolved on support ticket for now. will reopen if customer sees anything else. :thumbsup:
